lines.text: Your phone can find you anywhere on Earth without sending anything to space. It just listens to clocks.
Around thirty GPS satellites circle twenty thousand kilometers up, each carrying atomic clocks.
Each one keeps broadcasting the exact time, and where it is.
Your phone measures how late each signal arrives. Times the speed of light, that's your distance to the satellite.
One distance leaves you anywhere on a huge circle. Add more satellites, and the circles meet at one spot.
It needs at least four, because the fourth fixes the error in your phone's own cheap clock.
Here's the twist. Up there, time runs faster, about thirty eight millionths of a second a day.
Ignore Einstein, and GPS would drift about eleven kilometers a day. So the clocks are tuned slow before launch.
